transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is… I’ve been having a hard time sitting still. It’s not like I’m trying to be disruptive or anything, but when I’m in staff meetings, or even church event briefings, it feels like there’s a motor kind of humming under my skin. I end up shifting around, standing up, or finding some reason to move. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been noticeable enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Did this restlessness start after you began taking any psychiatric medication?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not really sure exactly what would count, but I haven’t noticed it starting after any kind of psychiatric medicine. As far as I can tell, it doesn’t seem tied to that.
Have you had times when you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

I don’t think so… not “high,” exactly. I mean, I have times where I’m more keyed up or busy, but I wouldn’t say it feels unusually energized compared to myself. Unless you mean something different by that?
As a child, were you often described as fidgety or unable to stay seated?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t trying to be a bad kid, but I do remember getting in trouble in grade school for popping up out of my seat and talking over the teacher sometimes. I’d rush ahead before they were even done giving directions.

My mom used to say I was kind of “wound too tight,” even when I was little. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Does this trouble sitting still happen in more than one setting, like at work, at home, and in social situations?

Yeah, it’s not just one place. I mean, I try not to make a big deal out of it, but if I’m supposed to sit still—like in staff meetings, or those church event briefings—I get this feeling like there’s a motor humming under my skin. I’ll shift around a lot, or stand up if I can, or find some little excuse to go move around. At home too, if I’m sitting too long. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
When you feel restless, is it usually because you’re worrying about something?

Not usually, no. I mean, I can worry like anyone, but that restless feeling is more like… when I’m expected to sit still, I get this motor kind of humming under my skin. Like in staff meetings or church briefings, I’ll start shifting around, or I’ll stand if that’s okay, or find some little reason to move. I’m not trying to be disruptive or anything—it just feels hard to stay put.
Do you often have trouble sustaining attention, like staying focused through meetings, reading, or tasks?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean… I can usually get through things if I need to, especially if I know someone’s counting on me. Meetings aren’t my favorite, but I wouldn’t want to say I can’t pay attention or anything.

Could you maybe say what you mean by “trouble sustaining attention”? Like, do you mean zoning out completely, or just having to work a little harder to stay with it?
Do you often find that your mind wanders and you lose track of what’s being said during meetings or conversations?

I don’t think that happens a lot, at least not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, sometimes in a long meeting I might have to kind of pull myself back to what’s being said, but I think most people do that, right?

In conversations, I usually try to keep up, especially if someone’s talking directly to me. I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Do you often interrupt people or answer before they’ve finished speaking?

Sometimes, yeah… I don’t mean to be rude. Like if my supervisor or someone at church is giving me instructions, I’ll kind of jump in with what I think they’re about to say before they’re done. I’m trying to be helpful, I guess, or show I understand.

But sometimes I’ve guessed wrong, and then they have to correct me. It’s a little embarrassing. I try not to do it.
Do you often misplace things you need, like your keys, phone, paperwork, or appointments?

Not that I can think of in any big way. I mean, everybody misplaces keys now and then, I guess, but I don’t think it’s something people are usually having to point out to me.

With appointments, I try to keep those written down or on my phone, so… I think I do okay with that. If that’s what you mean, I wouldn’t say it’s a major problem for me.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

I don’t know that I’d say I worry a lot for no reason. I mean, I think about bills, work, family stuff—normal things, I guess. But if there isn’t really something going on, I’m usually not sitting there worrying just out of nowhere.

At least, I don’t think so. If I’m understanding what you mean.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports ADHD with predominantly hyperactive/impulsive features: lifelong history since childhood of fidgetiness, leaving seat, blurting out/answering before instructions are completed, and current restlessness across multiple settings. Inattention symptoms were not clearly endorsed, but hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are persistent and impairing enough to prompt evaluation. Alternative explanations queried in the interview were not supported: symptoms were not linked to psychiatric medication, generalized worry was denied as the main driver, and there was no evidence of a manic/hypomanic state.
